01-token-distribution: Empirical cumulative distribution of whole-trajectory total-token reductions in 192 matched pairs, including flat zero and unity tails across the displayed domain. Positive values mean fewer EAL tokens. Two pairs have negative reductions and 190 have positive reductions; the median is 35.74%.
02-token-subgroups: Two pooled ratio-of-total-token reductions in each of four assigned recipient model/tool groups, each containing 48 matched trajectories. Blue squares include donor plus ten recipients; orange triangles include ten recipients only. The whole/recipient percentages are plain without tools 43.9/43.0, plain with tools 22.8/20.4, reasoning without tools 35.5/33.8, and reasoning with tools 40.8/39.5. Donors are pooled across both donor models with native tools.
03-cumulative-tokens: Ordinary and EAL cumulative input plus output tokens are shown from the donor through ten recipients, aggregated over 192 trajectories per arm. The horizontal coordinate is task-session position rather than wall-clock time. Ordinary ends at 2,982,385 tokens and EAL at 1,980,029.
04-token-composition: Eight horizontal bars compare ordinary and EAL token use in recipient sessions only for each recipient model and tool setting. Each bar aggregates 480 recipient sessions from 48 trajectories and partitions input, output minus reasoning, and reasoning output. Plain recipients have zero reasoning output. Donor usage is intentionally excluded.
05-resource-ratios: EAL divided by ordinary whole-run resource ratios show tokens down 33.6%, recorded API price subtotal down 23.3%, API attempts down 2.7%, client-observed API-call time down 8.6%, summed session and setup time up 8.5%, native acquisitions down 11.5%, and all acquisitions up 166.9%. These measures use distinct operational boundaries and units.
06-latency-distribution: Empirical distribution of EAL minus ordinary summed session plus setup time in 192 matched trajectories, with full zero and unity tails. Positive values mean higher EAL accumulated time. 138 pairs have positive differences and the median difference is 3.01 seconds; this is not workflow wall-clock duration.
07-acquisition-horizon: Cumulative evidence acquisitions and snapshot reuses from the donor through ten recipients across 192 trajectories per arm. At the final horizon EAL has 1,724 acquisitions, including 1,152 host acquisitions; ordinary has 646. EAL also has 960 host reuses, shown separately and excluded from acquisition totals. The reuse pattern follows deliberately authored assessment timing including the inclusive 60-second validity boundary.
08-measurement-status: Five rows count the same 4,224 sessions in the original finish recording and AI-coding snapshot, before the supplemental review. Completed sessions, resource records and AI-coded entries each number 4,224 and overlap. Resolved decisions number 4,199 and ambiguous decisions 25; only these last two rows form an additive partition. Ambiguities comprise 12 ordinary and 13 EAL sessions. Coding entries and resolved codes do not establish independent adjudication or measured assessor error.
09-paired-tradeoff: Scatter of paired total-token reductions against differences in summed session and setup time for 192 whole trajectories. Each percentage uses 100(1 - EAL total tokens / ordinary total tokens) within the matched trajectory. Zero lines separate four quadrants: 136 pairs have fewer EAL tokens and higher summed time, 54 fewer tokens and lower time, two more tokens and higher time, and zero more tokens and lower time. Squares and triangles identify assigned plain and reasoning recipients; no trend is fitted.
10-phase-contrasts: Three phase markers show pooled reductions for total tokens, API attempts, native probe calls, and summed session time. Blue squares denote donor, orange triangles ten recipients, and grey crosses their whole sum. Positive values mean lower EAL use. Recipient API attempts and native calls rise despite whole-run decreases. Session setup is excluded consistently from all phase timing ratios.
11-time-partition: Upper horizontal bars partition summed session time into client-observed API attempts, context construction, and a positive arithmetic residual. The EAL total is 5,597.7 seconds and ordinary 5,166.3 seconds. Neutral black marks in the lower panel use a separately labelled scale for sequence setup, 9.933 and 0.403 seconds respectively. The partition covers 2,112 sessions per arm and setup 192 sequences per arm.
12-recipient-decisions: Two count matrices compare authored reference decisions with AI-coded communicated decisions in the original finish coding snapshot, for 1,920 recipient sessions per arm. Rows ready, not ready and undetermined contain 768, 512 and 640 references. Columns ready, not ready, undetermined and ambiguous retain all 10 ordinary and 13 EAL recipient ambiguities. Ordinary row counts are 477/98/189/4, 291/84/131/6 and 362/100/178/0; EAL counts are 758/10/0/0, 2/508/0/2 and 6/23/600/11. Ready communications against non-ready references total 653 ordinary versus eight EAL. Shared tone encodes the percentage within each reference row. Agreement remains conditional on AI coding.
13-recipient-match-bounds: Four recipient model/tool groups in the original finish coding snapshot compare ordinary and EAL reference-match ambiguity ranges, each from 480 actual recipient sessions per arm and 48 matched trajectories. Ordinary ranges in plain/off, plain/on, reasoning/off and reasoning/on groups are 38.54, 37.50–39.58, 38.75 and 39.17 percent. EAL ranges are 99.79–100, 92.08–93.12, 98.96–100 and 97.92–98.33 percent. Orange triangles denote ordinary and blue squares EAL at the lower known-match share. Ranges assign unresolved codes to mismatches or matches while holding resolved AI codes fixed; they are not sampling intervals or assessor-error bounds.
14-frozen-endpoint-bounds: Three separately scaled panels retain the original finish coding snapshot and distinguish black finite-record observed coding ranges or an exact token point, grey two-sided family intervals and blue one-sided component lower bounds with rightward rays. The recipient EAL-minus-ordinary match difference has observed 58.18–59.38 percentage points, family 41.50–76.05 and one-sided lower 46.47, against a minus-five-point criterion. EAL match has observed 97.19–97.86 percent, family 88.71–100 and one-sided lower 91.22, against 90 percent. Donor-inclusive token reduction is 33.61 percent, family 32.33–34.89 and one-sided lower 32.74, against 20 percent. Inference uses 192 paired whole trajectories across 48 fixed strata with four raw reruns each. All one-sided criteria pass conditionally; the EAL family lower bound crossing 90 answers a different inferential question. The one-sided lower bounds are not simultaneously 95 percent covered, resolved-coder error is unbounded, and the original finish allocation report remains blocked by only two fully scored paired reruns in the least-complete cell.
